title: Agent Council
markdown:
The Executive (`openexecutive.orchestrator.executive.Executive`) is a single coherent persona that fans out to specialist sub-agents via Anthropic tool use. Each specialist subclasses `openexecutive.agents.base.BaseAgent`, carrying a `name`, `domain`, and `model`, and exposes `analyze(...)`, which wraps the question in user-turn context and calls Claude through the per-call provider.

Routing uses one `consult_specialist` tool. Beside it the Executive carries its skill tools (`search_skills`, `load_skill`, `create_skill`, `update_skill`, `delete_skill` — shown to users as **playbooks**; `create_skill` / `update_skill` / `delete_skill` never change the library — they save a draft (`knowledge/skill_drafts.py`) that a person approves on the Playbooks tab, and the reply links to it; `update_skill` / `delete_skill` (and `create_skill`, for a name a workflow still follows) refuse any built-in name (including a company's customized copy) and any company playbook a workflow (even a switched-off custom one) follows — workflows read playbooks at run time, approved scheduled ones included, and this loop also runs on inbound email and chat, so only a person on the Playbooks tab can change what a workflow follows; a hidden built-in is invisible to search and load; each `search_skills` hit lists the `workflows` that follow it, and the persona routes "the finished deliverable" to that workflow and quick or partial asks to the playbook inline); Tool calls made while proactive work is tagged (scheduler dispatch, reflection, research, alert review) feed the Attunement outcome ledger. Attunement adds `list_open_loops` (what a person owes — everyone's for the principal only in a private conversation, otherwise the caller's own) and `close_open_loop`, which only closes a loop when the turn's resolved speaker is the principal or the loop's owner — an unrostered sender, a signed-in web user not on the roster, and unattended sessions are refused. The roster write tools (`upsert_person`, `archive_person`, `set_department_head`) are the principal's alone, and only on a surface that verified the speaker — the web chat, the principal's own Slack or Discord, or a private Telegram chat when `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set to a value Telegram can send (Telegram identifies the chat rather than the sender, and without that secret its webhook accepts anyone's update). A teammate, an email (even from the principal's address), Google Chat, the CLI, the MCP server and unattended runs get `status: refused` (audited, and no action chip), because a People row is also the web sign-in and outbound-email allow-list. Multiple parallel `tool_use` blocks in a single assistant turn fan out concurrently through `router.route_parallel`, each running its own domain-filtered ChromaDB query before the specialist sees the question. The fan-out is failure-isolated per call: a specialist that raises or returns no text becomes an `UNAVAILABLE` tool_result (`router.specialist_unavailable_result`) instead of failing the whole turn, and its area — "finance", "legal", never the specialist's name — is reported to the user under the web reply, or by the Executive in its reply on other channels. Cancellation (Stop) still propagates. The Executive then synthesizes the returned analyses into one reply.

The nine entries in `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY` (`openexecutive.orchestrator.router`):

| Key | Agent | Domain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cso` | `StrategyAgent` | strategy |
| `cfo` | `FinanceAgent` | finance |
| `chro` | `HRAgent` | hr |
| `gc` | `LegalAgent` | legal |
| `coo` | `OperationsAgent` | operations |
| `cmo` | `MarketingAgent` | marketing |
| `cpo` | `ProductAgent` | product |
| `board_comms` | `BoardCommsAgent` | board |
| `triage` | `TriageAgent` | triage |

Models: specialists default to `claude-sonnet-5`; a deep-reasoning tier uses `claude-opus-5` (adaptive thinking); routing/fast classification uses `claude-haiku-4-5`. The Council's **Deep reasoning** toggle is honoured on Claude Opus/Sonnet (direct or via OpenRouter) and on any OpenRouter model whose live catalog entry supports `reasoning` (today all OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and Grok entries; not Llama) — the request translator turns Anthropic adaptive thinking + effort into OpenRouter's `reasoning` parameter. It is a silent no-op on models that can't reason, and disabled for Haiku, which rejects adaptive thinking. The Council picks a model in two steps: a **Provider** dropdown (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, xAI, Local, …), then a **Model** dropdown limited to that provider, with readable names ("Claude Opus 5.5") and the raw id and serving route shown underneath. The Anthropic group combines the direct Claude models (`claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`) with any Claude generation that exists only on OpenRouter, and never lists a model twice. With `OPENROUTER_ENABLED`, the non-Anthropic entries come from OpenRouter's live `/models` catalog (fetched at startup, refreshed in the background, filtered to tool-capable paid text models from an allowlisted vendor set), falling back to a built-in snapshot if the fetch fails. Eight Council-only agents are model/prompt-overridable in the UI but NOT callable via `consult_specialist`, because they are deliberately kept out of `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY`: `quality_judge` (committee review), `utility_fast` (gates, titles, decision parsing), `research` (the `executive_research` fan-out), `fixture_generator` (invents demo companies), `engagement_intake` (models a real client from intake material), `onboarding_interviewer` (interviews a new user about their own company and drafts its profile, people and departments), `workflow_designer` (runs the conversational New workflow wizard on `/jobs/new`: searches the available tools, asks clarifying questions, then drafts a validated dynamic-workflow definition for the user to review), and `workflow_actor` (runs a workflow's `action` steps: a bounded tool-use loop limited to the tools the user approved for that step). `fixture_generator`, `engagement_intake` and `onboarding_interviewer` share one shape — a forced tool call producing a whole company, validated for referential integrity, with a single repair retry — but opposite epistemics: the fixture author invents, the other two extract and leave unstated facts empty rather than guessing.

One more structured-output utility agent sits beside `triage`: `openexecutive.agents.alert_review.AlertReviewAgent` (routing model, one forced `emit_alert_reviews` tool call, never raises). The alert review job hands it a batch of open alerts with evidence and gets back, per alert, a verdict (relevant / changed / resolved / stale), a confidence, the evidence it relied on, a one-line note, why-now, an optional deadline, and a recommended move (none / route / nudge / escalate / draft / suggest_workflow / merge / close) with its parameters. Like `triage`, it never mutates state — `alerts.review.apply_verdict` executes the verdicts deterministically within authority, so the model's job is judgment, not action.

Every specialist *advises* — each returns domain analysis the Executive synthesizes into one voice. None of them act on the company's behalf; the side-effecting tools in the main loop (schedule, people, departments, broadcast, watchlist, workflows) belong to the Executive, not to a specialist.

The Executive can also launch *any* workflow conversationally: `orchestrator.workflow_run_tools` adds `list_workflows` (the launchable catalog with each workflow's inputs) and `run_workflow` (runs a built-in or custom workflow to completion and returns its artifact, checkpointing approval gates as `awaiting_human`). This makes the `/jobs` catalog reachable from chat — see the Workflows section.

Deliverables are first-class too. `orchestrator.artifact_tools` gives the Executive three tools: `draft_artifact` publishes a memo, web page (`html`), Word document (`docx`), spreadsheet (`xlsx`, from structured `sheets`) or a `link` to something it created in one of the principal's connected apps through the generic MCP gateway (`search_tools` → `call_tool`, any server — no vendor is named), and returns the artifact's id and link; `list_artifacts` and `get_artifact` let it find and reread its own past work (drafts and workflow outputs alike, through the same `artifact_records` read model the API uses). Revising is `draft_artifact(supersedes=<id>)`, which archives the earlier version. When the principal asks for a deliverable the tool is always used; the "quiet is the right default" bar applies only to unprompted drafts. The format enum is a hard-coded sorted tuple so the cached tool schema stays byte-stable. Delivery: `message_person(person_id, text, artifact_id?)` appends the artifact's title and a `UI_BASE_URL/artifacts/<id>` link (through the same outbound guard as any DM; the link needs Open Executive access), and a Gmail send/draft can attach the file itself by `artifact_id` — see Integrations.

The Executive also backs the **Ask OE** panel's form-fill tier via `orchestrator.form_tools.propose_form_values`: when a chat turn arrives with a `<page_context>` block describing a form on the user's screen, the Executive can propose values for it. The proposal is delivered to the UI as a `form_patch` SSE event and placed into the form as highlighted suggestions — the tool never saves or submits anything; the user reviews and saves manually. The tool is **always** in the tool list (tool definitions sit at the top of the cached prompt prefix, so a conditionally-present tool would invalidate the prompt cache whenever panel and non-panel turns alternate); its description restricts usage to turns that carry a form descriptor.
